title: Silverpine embed hosting throughput and compliance discovery
topics: hosting options: hosted vs dedicated vs private
summary: Discovery call with Silverpine Media to qualify embedding+rerank requirements. Key constraints: 100M docs, target 300 QPS, sub-150ms p99 rerank, EU data residency and Vault KMS, considering Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. SE to run sample throughput bench; AE to send pricing and security pack.
action_items: Leo Patel (Redwood) - run 300 QPS sample bench with 512d and 128d embeddings, share perf matrix - due 2025-03-07
Maya Chen (Redwood) - send security pack (SOC2 + data residency notes + KMS integration guide) and draft pricing options - due 2025-03-04
Tom Reynolds (Silverpine) - provide sample dataset (10k docs + typical query patterns) and index schema export - due 2025-03-05
next_steps: Redwood to run benchmark and share results
Schedule technical deep dive with infra team (Priya + Redwood SE)
Pilot contract discussion after bench validates p99
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-01 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~64m | Attendees: Maya Chen, Leo Patel (Redwood); Aisha Khan, Tom Reynolds, Priya Mehta (Silverpine)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a sec, um quick intros from our side. i'm maya, i'm the account lead.
[00:07] Leo (Redwood SE): leo here, infra and perf stuff, i'll be looking at throughput and the bench.
[00:12] Aisha (Silverpine): aisha, head of search at silverpine. we pipe search for our editorial and ad systems.
[00:17] Tom: tom, platform eng, i run the index infra.
[00:20] Priya: priya on security/compliance.
[00:22] Maya: great. objective for today's call is to understand your embedding + rerank needs, constraints, and what would make you pick hosted vs dedicated vs private.

[00:35] Aisha: yeah, high level: we have ~100M articles and assets, not all indexed but the candidate set is big. our current stack is elasticsearch with the dense-vector plugin, plus an in-house rerank microservice that calls a transformer on rerank stage. cost is creeping and tail latency spikes during peak editorial hours.

[00:55] Leo: good context. what's the target qps and tail latency you're aiming for on the rerank path?

[01:02] Aisha: target 300 qps peak, ideally p95 under 80ms and p99 under 150ms for the rerank result set — that's strict because editorial users need fast refresh.

[01:15] Tom: also multi-region; EU data residency required for some content. prefer solutions that can pin model serving in eu-west.

[01:23] Priya: security: we are SOC2 in progress, use HashiCorp Vault for keys, require audit logs, SSO via Okta/SAML. we need KMS integration and auditability before pilot.

[01:40] Maya: that all makes sense. quick question — are you generating embeddings in-house or using a managed embed service?

[01:46] Aisha: currently in-house using a slightly modified open model; embeddings are 512 dims. but we're exploring compact/quantized embeddings (e.g., 128d or 64d float16/quant) to reduce storage and speed up ANN.

[01:59] Leo: okay — tradeoffs there are expected: lower dims reduce index size and ANN latency but can hit recall. we typically recommend evaluating 512 vs 128 dims on your queries. for hosting, do you have a timeline for pilot?

[02:12] Tom: hoping to start a pilot in April, production end of Q3 ideally. budget TBD but we need predictable unit economics.

[02:20] Maya: great. to clarify hosting options: Redwood Hosted is fastest to onboard with managed model + endpoint; Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with isolation and predictable throughput; Redwood Private gives a VPC or on-prem control plane if you need full network separation and data never leaves your cloud.

[02:40] Aisha: for us, private sounds attractive because of residency + Vault keys. but dedicated could be okay if we can lock region and KMS integration. cost delta is also important.

[02:52] Priya: question on KMS — can Redwood integrate with our Vault for model keys and audit logs? we cannot expose keys to third parties.

[03:00] Leo: short answer: yes for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can be done with customer-managed KMS if we do a private endpoint and key wrapping; we need to validate with security team. audit logs are available in all tiers, though retention and export formats differ. we'll send the security pack with details.

[03:25] Aisha: cool. on vector DB side — we'd like to keep ES for now but add a fallback to a specialized ANN for rerank. any recommendations?

[03:34] Leo: a common pattern is hybrid: first-pass recall with ES/term match, then ANN fanout to an index (Faiss/Milvus/Pinecone), then rerank via model. Redwood can host the model endpoints and integrate with your ANN — we have connectors and examples for Faiss and cloud vector stores. also automatic KV prefix caching to reuse previous rerank cache on repeated queries.

[03:56] Tom: latency concern — if we fanout to an external vector DB, added network hops matter. can Redwood colocate model servers with the vector index?

[04:05] Leo: with Dedicated or Private, yes — we can place model serving in the same region or VPC and recommend colocating to minimize cross-network hops. for Hosted, we can choose region affinity but can't colocate in customer VPC. that's the main difference.

[04:20] Aisha: curious about quantization — if we go 128d quantized to int8 or 4-bit, what's typical p99 improvement? any back-of-envelope?

[04:30] Leo: quantization reduces memory and bandwidth; p99 for ANN lookup often drops 20-40% depending on ANN type and search params. but recall can drop. we should run an eval with your sample queries to show precision/recall vs latency and cost.

[04:45] Priya: we also need to know about model version pinning and rollbacks — can't afford silent regressions in rerank quality.

[04:52] Maya: Redwood supports model version pinning and can do canary rollouts with automatic fallback to a stable model. we also tie evals to prompt sets and can alert on regressions.

[05:05] Tom: on throughput: are there published bench numbers for 512d embeddings reranking 10 results at 300 qps?

[05:12] Leo: we have internal perf profiles but they vary by model and GPU. realistically for a 512d rerank on a T4-class GPU you'd need to batch and run multiple workers; Dedicated nodes with autoscaling are common. we'll run a tailored bench — we ask you for a 10k-doc sample and representative query mix.

[05:33] Aisha: ok we'll provide sample. question on cost model: how do you bill embeddings vs generation vs dedicated capacity?

[05:40] Maya: Hosted is usage-based (per-embedding/per-token), Dedicated is reserved hourly/GPU with overage, Private is license plus support. we'll include example cost models in the deck.

[05:52] Tom: any gotchas for integrating with our CI/CD? we deploy infra via terraform and our indices are provisioned by the platform team.

[05:59] Leo: we have terraform modules and k8s manifests for Private/Dedicated and API-first integration for Hosted. we can provide a quickstart repo.

[06:10] Priya: ok on compliance: retention of logs, ability to redact PII, and exportable audit trails — can you confirm?

[06:18] Maya: yes — audit logs export, redact hooks, and data retention controls exist. we'll include retention windows and export formats in the security pack.

[06:30] Aisha: any customer references in media/publishing that did a similar migration?

[06:36] Maya: we have a publishing customer (anonymized) who went from ES-only to hybrid with Dedicated, improved p99 and lowered cost per query — we'll include that reference in email.

[06:45] Tom: good. i have a technical nit: for rerank we typically do cross-encoder scoring which is costly for 10x fanout. any suggestions to reduce load?

[06:55] Leo: options: 1) use asymmetric rerank (bi-encoder candidate + lightweight cross-encoder on top-k), 2) reduce dims or quantize for faster ANN so you can increase recall without huge cross-encoder costs, 3) use caching for repeated queries. also batching requests internally lowers overall GPU cost.

[07:15] Aisha: sounds like we need an eval matrix: recall vs latency vs cost across embedding dims (512/128/64), quantization modes, and hosting tiers.

[07:24] Maya: agreed. action items: redwood runs bench with 512 and 128 dims at target 300 qps, share perf matrix; redwood sends security pack and pricing; silverpine shares sample dataset and queries.

[07:40] Priya: last question: do you do contract-level data residency guarantees for Hosted?

[07:47] Maya: Hosted can offer region pinning and contractual commitments for data location, but Private is the strongest guarantee. we'll detail options in the security pack and legal team can follow up.

[07:58] Tom: ok thanks. can we schedule follow-up technical deep dive focusing on KMS and bench results?

[08:03] Maya: yes — we'll propose slots after bench completes.

[08:10] Aisha: great, thanks everyone.

[08:15] (end)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mislabels and dropped punctuation; some filler words (um, yeah).
